title: From volunteer to town councillor, with the Council Climate Action Scorecards
content:
Kiran Crawford volunteered for the Council Climate Action Scorecards — and now he’s a town councillor, using everything the Scorecards taught him about local authorities’ powers to take climate action.

Kiran was elected as a Green councillor for Royal Leamington Spa Town council in July 2026. Prior to that, as a longtime volunteer with Climate Emergency UK, he helped make the Scorecards a reality.

“I originally volunteered for the first iteration of the Scorecards back in 2021, after hearing about them from a friend who had also signed up as a volunteer.

“Having been involved in some climate campaigning before, I was looking for more ways to support good policy. The Scorecards sounded like a great way to find out how good councils’ plans were, and I thought they could be really helpful tool in campaigning for action, so I signed up to help with the assessments.

“I found the process really interesting, and learnt a lot about what powers councils have around climate. Given how useful I could see the Scorecards would be, I then volunteered as a media amplifier to help get the launch out to the press, so that they could reach as many people as possible.
